items.event_time_ist: Evening of Oct 13, 2026 (Atlanta Press Club; morning of Oct 14, 2026 IST)
items.summary: Second Georgia Senate debate (Atlanta Press Club, Tuesday night Oct 13, 2026): Sen. Jon Ossoff and Rep. Mike Collins clashed over Jeffrey Epstein files. Collins attacked Ossoff over donations from Reid Hoffman ('The Epstein class is on stage right now, and it's you'); Ossoff shot back that Collins voted to 'cover up the evidence' and that 'Donald Trump, who, by the way, is named 1,000 times in the Epstein files.' Ossoff also said he has 'zero interest' in running for president in 2028 and will serve a full six-year term. Other flashpoints: Collins on immigration and green-energy backing; Ossoff tying Collins to Trump tariffs, the Iran war, and pressing him on a House ethics probe into misuse of taxpayer funds. Corroborated WSJ + CNN (plus Mediaite clip) = confirmed.
items.title: Georgia Senate debate: Ossoff, Collins trade Epstein-files attacks; Ossoff rules out 2028 run

items.event_time_ist: Oct 13, 2026, 7 PM ET (early morning of Oct 14, 2026 IST); WABI/WAGM, third of four debates
items.summary: Maine's third Senate debate (WABI/WAGM, Tue Oct 13, 7 PM ET): Sen. Susan Collins repeatedly distanced herself from Trump — criticizing his Iran war plan ('did not have a good plan,' should have anticipated the Strait of Hormuz closure), her vote against his 'One Big Beautiful Bill' over Medicaid cuts, and Canada tariffs — while touting her Appropriations chair as leverage to work with the administration. Heating oil (up ~80% year over year) was a major clash: Collins blamed Jackson and Augusta, Jackson blamed the Iran war. Anti-corruption exchange: Jackson raised the ProPublica pay-to-play allegation (Collins: 'political hit job,' 'categorically false'); Collins hit Jackson on his campaign's FEC report, which he promised 'tomorrow morning' ahead of Thursday's filing deadline. Corroborated CNN + USA Today (3 takeaways) = confirmed.
items.title: Maine Senate debate: Collins distances from Trump as heating oil and Iran war dominate

items.event_time_ist: Oct 13, 2026, 9 PM CT (morning of Oct 14, 2026 IST); WHO-13/Nexstar, final scheduled debate
items.summary: Iowa's final Senate debate (WHO-13/Nexstar, Tue Oct 13, 9 PM CT) for the open seat: Rep. Ashley Hinson hammered state Rep. Josh Turek for missing 58% of Iowa House floor votes this session ('two out of every five days of work'); Turek said he was campaigning in all 99 counties and countered that Hinson missed 150+ House votes. On her net worth, Hinson said 'I'm not trading stocks' — her husband sold his insurance business and their publicly traded stocks, though disclosures show $1-5M in privately held High Street Insurance stock. Both candidates opposed Trump's Russian diesel deal to lower gas prices; Hinson noted she is banned from Russia and lobbied Trump personally last week for soybean trade pacts. Iowa early voting starts today, Oct 14; RCP average has Turek +0.6. Corroborated Des Moines Register + CNN + KCAU = confirmed.
items.title: Iowa's final Senate debate: Hinson, Turek clash on missed votes, stock trading; both oppose Russian diesel deal

items.event_time_ist: Published Oct 12, 2026 (America PAC spokesperson confirmed the figures Oct 12; three days before the FEC disclosure deadline)
items.summary: Elon Musk's America PAC confirmed to reporters Oct 12 that he has poured at least $276 million into the midterms since July (Reuters: $366 million this cycle overall), making him likely the single-biggest political donor. Breakdown: $158M to the Senate Leadership Fund, $76M to America PAC's own GOTV effort across 7 Senate battleground states and nearly 3 dozen House races, $20M to the Congressional Leadership Fund, $10M to Lone Star Liberty PAC (backing Ken Paxton in the TX Senate race), $10M to the RGA and $2M to RAGA. This reverses his May 2025 pledge to spend 'a lot less' on politics; Trump honored Musk with the National Medal of Science last week. Corroborated CNN + NY Post (original reporting, new breakdown) + Reuters = confirmed.
items.title: Elon Musk confirmed as top GOP donor: $276M since July ($366M this cycle) to rescue Republican majorities

items.summary: Reuters special report published Oct 14: based on interviews with 50+ election officials, voting experts and election lawyers, plus reviews of Trump's statements, court filings and federal agency actions, it maps nine scenarios in which the administration could test federal authority over the midterms — including fraud allegations, deployment of federal election monitors, ballot seizures, emergency powers, and delayed certification. It catalogs Trump's push to 'nationalize' voting, restrict mail ballots, deploy federal law enforcement on fraud claims, and his September convention remark urging supporters to 'cheat like hell.' Single-sourced (wire only — no second outlet in a different lean category found yet).
items.title: Reuters special report: nine ways the Trump administration could interfere with the midterms
